title: Spider 2.0-AIFunc: Extending Real-World Text-to-SQL to AI-Native SQL Workflows
hook: Cloud platforms let analysts call AI functions right inside SQL. Spider 2.0-AIFunc is the first benchmark testing whether models can write that kind of query — top models still cap out near 70%.
key_points: 465 verified instances across 125 real-world databases, covering six AI-native SQL function types on Snowflake.
Built by rewriting an existing enterprise text-to-SQL benchmark via an agent-based pipeline into AI-native form.
Every instance passes repeated execution across separated time windows to confirm answer stability before release.
Best proprietary models reach only 67-70% execution accuracy; the best open-source model manages 58.1%.
Agent frameworks built for classic text-to-SQL don't transfer here — a minimal agent setup matches or beats them.
content_html: Real analysts already write SQL that calls out to AI functions — classify this row, extract that entity, find similar text — right inside platforms like Snowflake. Spider 2.0-AIFunc is the first benchmark that tests whether models can actually generate that kind of query.
extra_html:
What's being tested

Built from an existing enterprise text-to-SQL benchmark, Spider 2.0-AIFunc rewrites 465 tasks across 125 real databases into AI-native form covering six function types — classification, filtering, sentiment analysis, extraction, similarity search, aggregation — on Snowflake's AI SQL functions. An agent-based pipeline handled the rewriting, and every instance was run repeatedly across separated time windows to confirm the expected answer stays stable before release.

What they found

The best proprietary models land at only 67-70% execution accuracy; the strongest open-source model manages 58.1%. Failures cluster around predicate specification, schema grounding, and getting the AI function's own parameters right, not just standard SQL logic. More surprising: agent frameworks built for classic text-to-SQL problems, like schema retrieval and table selection, don't transfer to this AI-native setting — a minimal, bare-bones agent setup matches or beats the elaborate ones. Liu, Xu, and colleagues, arXiv 2026.

flashcards.prompt: What's different about the SQL that Spider 2.0-AIFunc tests, versus classic text-to-SQL benchmarks?
flashcards.back_html: Queries invoke AI-native SQL functions — classification, extraction, similarity search, sentiment analysis, and more — inside otherwise ordinary SQL, not just standard relational operations.

flashcards.prompt: Where do models mostly fail on Spider 2.0-AIFunc, per the error analysis?

choices.text: Predicate specification, schema grounding, and parameterizing the AI functions themselves
Basic SQL syntax errors like missing keywords
Failing to connect to the Snowflake database at all

flashcards.explanation_html: The 67-70% ceiling for top proprietary models traces to getting predicates, schema references, and AI-function parameters right, not baseline SQL syntax.

flashcards.prompt: What did the authors find about elaborate agent frameworks on this benchmark?
flashcards.back_html: Frameworks built for traditional text-to-SQL challenges, like schema retrieval and table selection, didn't transfer — a minimal agent setup consistently matched or beat them.
